thread:
marie: Heads-up: p-prof on rtx-cluster shows KV cache fragmentation skyrockets under mixed-length convo batches. Seen ~28% wasted KV bytes and a couple of OOM spikes when prefill runs hot. Thinking about compact-on-evict vs prefill backpressure.

cj: 28% is huge. Can you paste the numbers (slot size distro / free vs used)?

marie: Sure — quick snapshot from p-prof: `total_kv=12.0GB`, `fragmented=3.4GB (28%)`, `avg_slot=48B`, `slots<64B=72%`, `prefill_ratio=0.63`. OOMs correlate with bursts of long-decoding requests.

devin: Two ideas: (1) compact-on-evict background pass that coalesces tiny free slots into larger ones before big prefill; (2) adaptive per-request prefill cap that is lowered when fragmentation is high so we don't worsen the hole problem.

cj: Compaction sounds promising but it's CPU / PCIe heavy and could stall decode if done inline. Maybe opportunistic/async compaction triggered by eviction events only, and rate-limited on a separate stream.

marie: Did a tiny sim locally: async compaction reclaim ~1.8GB over 60s with negligible p99 latency delta when scheduled at low QPS (<10k reqs/min). Will run microbench for heavier loads. Also thinking about a "demotion queue" to avoid endlessly prefilling the same hot keys that churn small slots.

devin: Cheap heuristic we can try immediately: if `prefill_ratio > 0.6` AND `slots<64B > 60%` then reduce per-request prefill cap by 30% and route those requests through a thin-evict fast-path. Low risk and reversible.

cj: Please add metrics we can watch: `kv_compact_time`, `kv_bytes_reclaimed`, `prefill_cap_delta`, `kv_small_slot_ratio`. Expose an experiment flag so we can toggle and measure.

marie: Will do. I'll open a PR with the microbench + an initial compact-on-evict prototype and the prefill-cap heuristic. Assigning to myself, will ping @devin for reviews on the heuristic. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
